facts.text: Woodbridge was named after Michigan Governor William Woodbridge, whose farm originally occupied the land.
The neighborhood has hosted Detroit legends such as Ty Cobb, David Stott, James Scripps, Meg White, Sixto Rodriguez, and George Booth.
Woodbridge’s streets are lined with historic homes that have been beautifully renovated into modern living spaces.
Each September, an annual Home and Garden Tour lets visitors stroll through the colorful homes and meet the residents who shape the area’s history.
The Contemporary Art Institute of Detroit and 4731 Gallery are two art institutions that call Woodbridge home.
Woodbridge’s digital archive preserves oral histories, personal collections, and newspaper clippings that celebrate the neighborhood’s rich past.
